question: Does the abbreviated Fr 10437 Domus mea cue establish that no complete Domus mea antiphon occurs in its service?
local_observation: Fr 10437 capture 2 provisionally reads the end of Lapides pretiosi, an abbreviated Domus me... / Domus or... cue, then an Ad bened... ant... rubric and Mane surgens. The cue and markers are unreviewed.
candidate_interpretation: The small cue may represent the verse-and-response work Cantus 008036, but the abbreviations and markers do not independently confirm the expansion or work ID.
published_control: Cantus index for Krakow Carmelite Ms.3 f.80r lists Lauds antiphons Domum tuam, Hec est domus, Domus mea, Bene fundata, Lapides; then a hymn, Domus mea verse 008036 and Mane surgens. An Utrecht Ms.406 index also places the full Domus mea antiphon and a later verse in the same Lauds service, but places the antiphon before Hec est domus.
consequence: A verse cue does not prove omission of the full antiphon, and a Domum–Hec opening can coexist with Domus later. Both are concrete published alternatives; neither inventory establishes the missing folded Swedish text or book identity.
limits: Reference-exposed AI image reading; source markers and exact spelling require independent checking. Krakow and Utrecht inventories accessed through indexed search text, not original manuscript images. There is intervening hymn material in Krakow; no exact full-sequence identity, transmission, prevalence or originality is established. Capture 1-to-2 physical continuity remains unverified.
next_test: Compare a securely corresponding notated antiphon across existing candidates and controls with explicit pitch and text underlay uncertainty, or inspect an authenticated source view exposing the folded section without retrying failed URLs.
